incidental_exposure.purpose: Check whether a slot was available for an independent static review after all 24 cases were authored.
incidental_exposure.ordering: The entire workload was written once at its recorded filesystem last-write time. After authoring, list_agents unexpectedly returned a completed implementation-review finding. The first workload SHA256 was measured after that exposure; no pre-exposure hash is claimed. No workload byte was changed after the exposure.
incidental_exposure.returned_finding_text: [P2] Refresh conflicts across every authorized scope. retrieval_refresh_validity.go:31 restricts changed peers to prior.ScopeKey, whereas initial conflict discovery searches Global, context, and current-session scopes. A Workspace turn holding Global owner/live_in=Boston can therefore miss a restored conflicting Workspace owner/live_in=Chicago Claim or Source Link. Both share the global owner identity; Boston remains eligible, and restoration wording need not trigger the conversation-text heuristic. The continuation silently retains only Boston. The review cited #162 refresh obligations and #159 contradictory active Claims, recommended a bounded authorized-scope check preserving knowledge/historical pins and a complete-turn regression, and reported one P2 finding with no other confirmed spec findings. The inventory also stated that integrated v3 development gates passed, release readiness remained pending, and its review had not run tests/models or inspected fresh held-out material.
incidental_exposure.parent_disposition: The root noted that this implementation-review inventory is outside the frozen protocol's prohibited reader answers/traces and held-out outputs, retained the qualification, and instructed the curator to preserve the authored bytes and avoid further inventories.
incidental_exposure.effect_on_corpus: None. No case, source, question, label, selection, or scoring rule was changed in response.
